site.tagline: The web studio with a rack — wire your tools like a synth.
site.hero.note: One line. The runtime is bundled. This page is being served to you by the app itself — look for the ⇄ chip on its status line.
site.hero.note.web: One line. The runtime is bundled. Open this same page from inside the app — Help ▸ NMOX Studio Website (local) — and it is served to you by the product itself, with the ⇄ chip to prove it.
site.loop.h: The loop that teaches is the loop that closes
site.loop.p: Edit, save, look — and when the page breaks, the error lands in your editor at the failing line, ORACLE explains it with your own source in front of it, and the tutorial checks your work. Doing, learning, and experimenting are the same motion here.
site.rack.h: A rack, not a run button
site.rack.p: Fifty-three devices — servers, test runners, gates, watchers, an AI error-explainer — mount on a rack and wire together with patch cables. A failing test can trigger its own explanation. A green build can gate a ship. Your own devices are one JSON file away.
site.learn.p: Learning spaces for languages, frameworks, and libraries — each with sample code, a walked tutorial, a live REPL, and checkpoints that verify what you built. Teachers export their own spaces as one file; students drop it in and press Check.
site.laws.l1: Refusals speak. Nothing fails silently, ever.
site.laws.l2: Secrets live in your keychain, never in a project file.
site.laws.l3: Nothing runs a stranger's code without asking you first.
site.laws.l4: Kits never clobber; wiring never doubles.
site.colophon: Built in NMOX Studio, checked by its own kits, served by its own rack. Apache-2.0.
site.shown.p: One toggle and every editor, the page in the in-app Browser, the Output window and the Terminal read from the back row — and come back exactly when you stop. The chord you press shows on screen; what you type never does. Code copies as a fenced block, or with the GitHub link to the same lines; the editor tab saves or copies as a crisp 2x image; the project tree pastes as a README.
